How to find an NHS rheumatologist near me in Northern Ireland — rheumatology services in Northern Ireland are provided through the five Health and Social Care (HSC) Trusts. Unlike England, there is currently no direct self-referral pathway for rheumatology — all referrals go through your GP.

Quick answer: NHS rheumatology in Northern Ireland: ask your GP to refer you to your nearest HSC Trust rheumatology department. Current waiting times are 12-24+ months for routine; urgent (new inflammatory arthritis) should be within weeks. Patient Client Council: 0800 917 0222 for waiting list rights.

The Five HSC Trust Rheumatology Departments

  • Belfast HSC Trust: Royal Victoria Hospital and Musgrave Park Hospital — the largest rheumatology centre in NI
  • Southern HSC Trust: Craigavon Area Hospital
  • South Eastern HSC Trust: Ulster Hospital, Dundonald
  • Northern HSC Trust: Antrim Area Hospital
  • Western HSC Trust: Altnagelvin Hospital, Derry/Londonderry

How to Get a Referral

Make an appointment with your GP and specifically request a rheumatology referral. NICE guidance recommends urgent referral within 3 working days for suspected new inflammatory arthritis. For established arthritis needing specialist review, routine referral is standard. Ask your GP to document that you have requested the referral and the clinical reason.

Arthritis consultation — openly licensed via Openverse

Waiting Times in NI

Northern Ireland has faced some of the longest NHS waiting times in the UK. As of 2026, routine rheumatology waits of 12–24+ months are reported. Urgent referrals should be seen faster — within weeks. If you have been waiting over 12 months without an appointment, contact the Patient Client Council (0800 917 0222) who can advise on your rights.

While You Are Waiting

  • Ask your GP to manage symptoms in the interim — NSAIDs, analgesics and physiotherapy referral can be arranged while waiting
  • Consider a private rheumatology consultation (£200–350 one-off) for a diagnosis and initial management plan
  • Contact Versus Arthritis NI (versusarthritis.org) for peer support

Q&A

Question: Can I choose which HSC Trust I am referred to?
Short answer: In Northern Ireland, choice of provider is more limited than in England. Your GP will usually refer to your nearest trust. You can ask about referral to a different trust if there are clinical reasons or significantly different wait times.

Question: What should I bring to my first rheumatology appointment?
Short answer: Full medication list, symptom diary (2–4 weeks minimum), blood test results your GP has already done, and a written list of your questions.

Practical next steps for How to Find an NHS Rheumatologist Near Me Northern Ireland

If you came here about How to Find an NHS Rheumatologist Near Me Northern Ireland, pick one change you can keep for a fortnight rather than overhauling everything at once. Note what hurts, what helps, and what you have already tried, then take that list to your GP, rheumatology nurse or physiotherapist so the conversation stays concrete.

In many areas you can ask your NHS trust about self-referral to physiotherapy or lifestyle support without waiting for a hospital letter. Check your GP surgery website or the NHS App for the route that applies where you live.

Reliable UK sources

Cross-check major decisions with NHS.uk, your clinical team, and NICE guidance summaries where relevant. Be wary of social posts that promise reversal of arthritis or attack standard medicines without evidence.

Pacing on good and bad days

On better days it is tempting to catch up on everything at once. Spread chores and exercise across the week instead. Use the two-hour rule many physiotherapists suggest: if pain or fatigue is clearly worse two hours after activity, the dose was too high — trim the next session rather than stopping altogether.

Quick questions about Find Rheumatologist Near Northern

Is this a substitute for seeing a clinician? No. Use it to prepare questions and understand options, then confirm decisions with your NHS team.

How long before I judge whether a change helped? Give most habit or exercise changes at least two to four weeks, unless pain or swelling clearly worsens — in that case scale back sooner.

What should I track? Joint pain (0–10), morning stiffness time, sleep quality, and how far you can walk or how long you can type or stand. Patterns beat one-off ratings.

Safety and when to get urgent help

This page is general information for people in the United Kingdom, not personal medical advice. Seek urgent help via NHS 111 or A&E if you have sudden inability to move a joint, hot swollen joint with fever, chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or symptoms that feel immediately dangerous.
